name: Germany
description:
Europe's largest economy with a strong engineering and technology sector. Germany offers excellent education, healthcare, and a rich cultural heritage spanning from Berlin to Bavaria.

## Key Highlights
- Strong economy and innovation hub
- Excellent education and healthcare systems
- Rich cultural heritage and world-class infrastructure
longdescription: Germany is Europe's largest economy and a global leader in engineering, automotive manufacturing, and technology innovation. With a population of over 83 million, Germany plays a central role in European politics and economics. The country is renowned for its engineering excellence, hosting world-famous companies like BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Siemens, and Deutsche Telekom. Germany's education system is highly regarded, with numerous universities consistently ranking among the world's best. The country offers universal healthcare, reliable public transportation, and excellent quality of life standards. Berlin, the capital, has transformed into a vibrant hub for startups and creative industries, while traditional manufacturing centers like Stuttgart and Munich remain economic powerhouses. German culture is rich and diverse, from world-class museums and classical music traditions to Oktoberfest celebrations. The country's commitment to environmental sustainability and the "Energiewende" (energy transition) makes it a leader in renewable energy adoption. German workers benefit from strong labor rights, generous social benefits, and excellent work-life balance. The cost of living is moderate compared to other Western European countries, though major cities are increasingly expensive. For skilled professionals, Germany offers numerous opportunities in manufacturing, technology, healthcare, and finance sectors.

visas.name: The EU Blue (Germany)
visas.description: The EU Blue Card is a work permit for highly qualified non-EU citizens, offering a pathway to permanent residence in Germany and the EU.

visas.name: Germany Student Visa (Studentenvisum)
visas.description: Germany's student visa (Studentenvisum) for non-EU nationals accepted into a German university or higher education institution for a full degree programme lasting more than 90 days.
benefits: Part-time work permitted up to 120 days/year
Tuition-free education at many public universities

visas.name: Germany Family Reunion Visa
visas.description: Germany's family reunion visa (Familienzusammenf�hrung) allows spouses, minor children, and in some cases dependent relatives of German residents and citizens to join them in Germany for long-term residence.

visas.name: Germany Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte)
visas.description: Germany's points-based Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) allows qualified non-EU nationals to enter Germany for up to one year to search for work or test the job market, without a prior job offer.
benefits: Enter Germany without a prior job offer
Work up to 20hrs/week whilst job seeking
Convert to work permit when employed

visas.name: Germany Job Seeker Visa
visas.description: Germany's job seeker visa allows highly qualified non-EU professionals with a recognised degree to enter Germany for up to six months to look for work matching their qualifications.
benefits: Search for work in Germany in person
Convert to work visa when employed

Citizenship by Descent.desc:
**One German parent:** Child acquires citizenship automatically at birth.

**Two foreign parents:** Child can acquire if one parent has permanent residence for 8 years.

Naturalization.desc:
**Requirements:** 8 years lawful residence (5 years for spouses), basic German language (B1), integration test, no criminal record, financial independence.

**Dual citizenship:** Generally not permitted but exceptions exist for children.

Spouse of German Citizen.desc: Spouses can naturalize after 3 years residence with 5-year total residency requirement, or 2 years if married before first residence.

Birthright Citizenship.desc: Limited jus soli: Only applicable to children of foreign residents under specific residency conditions.

Exceptional Naturalization.desc: Individuals with outstanding achievements in science, business, or culture may apply with reduced requirements.

tax_advice:
- Germany has progressive income tax rates (0% to 42%)
- Corporate tax (Körperschaftsteuer) is 30% plus trade tax
- VAT at 19% (reduced rates of 7% and 0% on essentials)
- Dual income taxation system between federal and state level
- Significant tax deductions available for business expenses
- Retirement and insurance contributions are tax-deductible
- Church tax of 8-9% applies if church member
- Wealth tax abolished, but inheritance tax applies
local_tips:
- German bureaucracy is efficient but thorough; keep all documents organized
- Register with local government (Anmeldung) within 2 weeks of arrival
- Healthcare system excellent; mandatory public or private insurance required
- Learn German quickly; English common but German essential for integration
- Apprenticeship and vocational training (Ausbildung) widely available
- Punctuality and directness highly valued in German culture
- Recycling is mandatory with strict sorting requirements
